essence: A clear mind after disciplined practice is the void, not confusion or ignorance.
modern_lens: The Void scroll makes one point: emptiness is not a lack of knowledge but a settled, uncluttered mind, built through daily practice, that sees things as they are. Modern work and personal decisions go wrong when unknowns get mistaken for impossibilities, or when our own preferences bend what we see. The remedy is honest mapping of what you know, daily practice that clears the noise, and a straight standard applied before you act.

principles.name: Unknown Is Not Void
principles.gloss: Not knowing is a gap to fill, not emptiness. Sort the open questions honestly into knowable, testable and unknowable, then act on the map.

principles.name: Clear the Clouds Daily
principles.gloss: Clear judgement is a practice, built day by day. Empty the noise first, then look at the situation as it actually is.

principles.name: A Straight Mind
principles.gloss: Personal bias bends even good views. Check your conclusions against plain, fixed standards before you commit.
